content:
marta: Morning — noticed last night's nightly-eval (run id 2145678901) shows a big quality drop for rwd-int4-v2 on the safety-qa prompt set. ~24% truthfulness drop and 18 timeouts out of 100 samples.
ci-bot: nightly job 2145678901 failed: worker exit 137 on runner-3, see https://ci.redwood/internal/jobs/2145678901
yves: quick skim of the harness logs — lots of 'throttled by cgroup' and repeated 'sched_yield' backoffs from worker-3. Not seen on fp16 baseline.
sherman: confirmed it's primarily the quantized INT4 nightlies. fp16 nightly stable.
anjali: I repro locally by spinning 8 eval workers with --batch-size=1. When host is unconstrained it's fine; when I artificially drop CPU quota the timeouts start appearing.
tomas: any infra changes recently around CPU pinning / quotas? We did a runtime tweak last week to set --cpu-shares for dedicated pools.
marta: log snippet: \n```[2026-03-19T02:31:12Z] worker-3: cgroup_throttle event, throttled_ns=1123000000 pid=2891\n[2026-03-19T02:31:12Z] worker-3: sample loop sleep 1.2s (expected < 10ms)\n[2026-03-19T02:31:13Z] watchdog: eval-task timeout after 120s, killing pid=2891\n```\nsherman: sounds like the watchdog is firing on wall-clock stalls caused by CPU steal. We use cpu-time timeout in some places, wall-clock in others — inconsistency could make things worse.
yves: I also saw intermittent large GC pauses in the Python harness (gc.collect ~200-400ms) but not nearly enough to hit 120s. GC + throttling combined could push bad cases over the edge.
anjali: quick mitigation: bump per-task timeout for quantized nightly runs from 120s -> 240s and add a retry in the harness. That will stop noisy regressions while we root cause.
tomas: I'll spin a staging run with cpu_quota=40% to attempt deterministic repro and collect perf counters (steal cycles, iowait, rq-sleep).
yves: I'll draft a small harness change to have watchdog prefer wall-clock timeouts for tasks that call external subprocesses, and fall back to cpu-time for pure compute. Opening PR now.
ci-bot: PR #4023 created by yves: test coverage updated + watchdog patch. Pipeline status: pending.
marta: thanks. For triage plan: (1) confirm repro in staging with enforced CPU throttling, (2) collect perf counters and docker stats, (3) audit recent runtime flags that touched cpu_shares/affinity, (4) land short-term timeout bump if staging repros.
sherman: also add a tiny harness metric for 'throttle_time_ms' so we can correlate with quality regressions over time.
tomas: ack, starting staging run now — will post results in this thread.
marta: tagging @eng-infra and @eng-sre for visibility :mag: — this looks like an infra-induced flake rather than a model regression.
